question_text: The preexponential and activation energy for the diffusion of chromium in nickel are $1.1 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{s}$ and 272,000 J/mol, respectively. At what temperature will the diffusion coefficient have a value of $1.2 \times 10^{-14} \mathrm{~m}^{2} / \mathrm{s}$ ?The unit of the answer is K.
response:
Using the Arrhenius equation $D = D_0 \exp\!\left(-\dfrac{Q_d}{RT}\right)$ and solving for temperature:

$$T = \frac{Q_d}{R \ln(D_0/D)}$$

With $D_0 = 1.1\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}$, $Q_d = 272{,}000\ \mathrm{J/mol}$, $D = 1.2\times10^{-14}\ \mathrm{m^2/s}$, and $R = 8.31\ \mathrm{J/(mol\cdot K)}$:

$$T = \frac{272000}{8.31\,\ln(1.1\times10^{-4}/1.2\times10^{-14})} \approx 1427\ \mathrm{K}$$

$$\boxed{1427}$$
